_comment: Home page 'Top 3's': the best parks for each activity, in order. Keys are activity slugs; park codes must exist in content/parks. 1–3 picks each; 'why' is the one-line reason shown on the card. Activities left out don't get a pill.

hiking.why: Angels Landing, The Narrows and Observation Point
Highline Trail and Grinnell Glacier through alpine country
Half Dome, the Mist Trail and Yosemite Valley's big walls

backpacking.why: Rim-to-rim across the canyon, camping at Phantom Ranch or Bright Angel
Wilderness coast, rainforest valleys and glaciated peaks in one park
Island wilderness on the Greenstone Ridge, reached only by boat or plane

camping.why: Lakeside campgrounds right under the Teton Range
Ten developed campgrounds in old-growth Appalachian forest
Blackwoods and Seawall, a short walk from the Atlantic shore

kayaking.why: Paddle among calving tidewater glaciers and humpback whales
A park that's mostly water: linked lakes and hundreds of islands
Sea caves and kelp forests off Santa Cruz Island

rafting.why: The Colorado River through the canyon: the classic multi-day trip
Some of the East's best whitewater on the New and Gauley rivers
Cataract Canyon's big rapids below the Green and Colorado confluence

paddleboarding.why: Glassy mornings on String and Leigh lakes
Calm summer days on Lake Michigan's dune shoreline
Warm, shallow, clear water across Biscayne Bay

boating.why: Houseboats and island campsites across the big lakes
A park that's 95% water, with keys, reefs and shipwrecks
Day boats deep into the fjords to the glacier faces

fishing.why: Native cutthroat trout in the Yellowstone and Lamar rivers
Snook, redfish and tarpon on the backcountry flats
Brooks River's salmon runs and big rainbow trout

rock-climbing.why: El Capitan and Half Dome: the birthplace of big-wall climbing
Thousands of granite routes and boulders in the desert
Hard sandstone sport and trad lines above the New River

mountaineering.why: Glaciated 14,410 ft summit, the standard US training ground
The Grand Teton's classic alpine routes

skiing.why: World-class backcountry lines in the Tetons
Spring corn and ski touring from Paradise
Backcountry bowls and couloirs off Trail Ridge and Bear Lake

cross-country-skiing.why: Groomed trails past steaming geyser basins in winter
Ski the rim of a snow-filled caldera
Quiet volcanic backcountry under deep snow

snowshoeing.why: Ranger-led snowshoe walks on the caldera rim
Paradise, one of the snowiest places on Earth
Bear Lake and Dream Lake routes in deep, reliable snow

ice-climbing.why: Frozen gullies and falls around Loch Vale
Glacier ice and crevasse skills on the mountain

mountain-biking.why: The White Rim Road: 100 miles of desert riding
Singletrack on the East Rim trail system
Remote backcountry roads across the Chihuahuan Desert

horseback-riding.why: Mule rides into the canyon from the rims
Guided rides down among the hoodoos
Trail rides along the Blue Ridge from Skyland

swimming.why: Trunk Bay and Cinnamon Bay's calm Caribbean water

snorkeling.why: Healthy coral and sea life right off the fort's moat wall
An underwater snorkel trail at Trunk Bay
Living reefs and the Maritime Heritage shipwreck trail

caving.why: The world's longest known cave system
The Big Room, one of North America's largest cave chambers
Rare boxwork formations under the prairie

wildlife-watching.why: Wolves, bison and grizzlies in the Lamar and Hayden valleys
Moose, caribou, Dall sheep and grizzlies along the park road
Brown bears fishing for salmon at Brooks Falls

stargazing.why: Some of the darkest skies in the lower 48
High desert air and a dark-sky park far from any city
Thousands of visible stars and ranger astronomy programs

scenic-driving.why: 105 miles of Skyline Drive along the Blue Ridge
Trail Ridge Road, the highest continuous paved road in the US

photography.why: Delicate Arch and the Windows at sunset
Oxbow Bend and Mormon Row at sunrise
Endless rim viewpoints in changing light
